ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT RAMP LABS

Ramp Labs is Ramp's AI research and engineering group. We post-train models on finance work, build the environments and evals they learn from, and ship them into the products 85,000+ companies use to move money.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Most agent work today is one agent, one trace, and a person reads the result. We're building systems where that stops working: thousands of agents fanned out over a large search space, each returning partial results, with an orchestrator that turns all of it into something useful: hundreds of merged PRs, a dataset, the input to another system, or something nobody has built yet.

You'll design and run those systems: how work gets split, how agents coordinate, how results get deduplicated, verified and ranked, and what it all costs. The problems are general (agent swarms, agentic map-reduce, long-running fan-out workflows) and you'll own them from prototype to production.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Decide how the work gets done: how to break a problem down, what each agent sees, how many agents to run, and which model handles which step

 - Squeeze accuracy out of the models: context design, self-verification, voting and consensus across agents, and knowing when more agents stop helping

 - Measure quality without reading every trace: sampling, automated verification, and precision and recall on the final output

 - Drive down cost and latency per useful result: model routing, caching, early stopping, and smaller or fine-tuned models where they hold up

 - Turn one-off experiments into reusable workflows on our existing orchestration stack

 - Evaluate new models, inference setups and training approaches, and bring in what works




WHAT YOU NEED

 - Experience building applied AI systems and LLM applications that shipped

 - Hands-on experience with multi-agent or high-fan-out LLM workloads: parallel agents, map-reduce over models, large batch inference

 - Strong engineering in Python; you build concurrent, distributed systems that hold up in production

 - Judgment about output: you decide what the end result should look like before you scale the swarm, and you can separate signal from agent noise

 - The habit of measuring: cost, yield, false-positive rate, and whether a change actually helped

 - Ownership: you can run a roadmap and a production system with little oversight

 - Clear written communication




NICE-TO-HAVE

 - Built agent orchestration or job systems (Ray, Temporal, Modal or custom)

 - Used LLMs to search large spaces: codebases, document sets, logs or other large corpora

 - Post-training or hosting open-source models for high-volume inference

 - Distributed systems background

 - Public work we can look at: an agent framework, an open-source project, a write-up or a paper

About the Role:

As an AI Forward Deployed ProcessOS is a new kind of Camunda product: business processes described in natural language, generated as executable BPMN workflows, and improved autonomously from production data. We’re hiring the first cohort of Forward Deployed Engineers to bring it into production at enterprise customers. You’ll own the deployment journey from first process file to a working, improving system, and hand off a functioning capability to the customer’s team. The code you write and the patterns you discover feed directly back into how ProcessOS is built. This is a rare opportunity to shape a product, a function, and a field practice from day one.


You’ll work end‑to‑end across Java services and React interfaces, collaborating closely with a talented global team to measure, improve, and scale performance and fault tolerance in real-world distributed systems.

What you'll be doing:

 -  Deploy and prove. Own the journey from first process file to production workflow. At 90 days: at least one workflow running, the improvement loop active, and measurable fitness gains the customer can see. At 12 months: 3–5 customers with viable deployments.

 - Drive organizational adoption. Work across technical and business stakeholders to build understanding and trust, turning early deployments into lasting customer capability.

 - Work at depth technically. Configure and run Camunda clusters locally and in cloud environments. Debug integration failures. Build custom agents where platform defaults don’t fit. Write connector logic that gets legacy enterprise systems talking to ProcessOS.

 - Build the playbook. There is no deployment template yet. Document what good looks like as you discover it, and make the next implementation faster.

 - Feed the product. Custom integrations you write get contributed back. Integration patterns get codified. Production bugs you find, you often fix. Your field work is a direct input to ProcessOS.

 - Hand off deliberately. Leave customers with a team that can operate independently, is trained on the platform, and acts on improvement results without you.

What you bring:

 - Ability and/or willingness to use our product https://accounts.cloud.camunda.io/signup?_ga=2.47330343.127558761.1654184528-504024057.1654184528.

 - Enterprise production experience: you’ve shipped something inside a large organization and stayed to see it operate. You know why governance and resilience matter at scale.

 - Technical depth: You can debug an integration failure, write a custom agent against a legacy API, stand up a Camunda cluster from scratch, and explain generated BPMN to both engineers and business leads.

 - Stakeholder communication: you work effectively across engineering, architecture, and business leadership and adapt how you communicate without losing precision.

 - Practical AI experience: you’ve used AI to solve real problems in production – not just experimented. You understand context management, prompt engineering, agent testing, and integration tradeoffs.

 - Comfort with ambiguity: you make sound judgment calls without a playbook and document what you learn.

 - Occasional travel may be required

Nice-to-haves:

 - Experience in a customer-facing engineering or professional services role.

 - Familiarity with regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, or insurance

 - Production experience with agentic systems or AI-integrated workflows.

 - Contributions to a shared platform or open source project that others built on.
